reference_logic: Prefer exact regional Flora direct account under 1999 printed names, modern Kew accepted names and GrassBase for other taxa; additional USGS, Texas A&M, UF IFAS, USDA and peer-reviewed genus study. Reuse old iNat visual notes without pretending new image inspection.
taxonomy_ambiguities: Dichanthelium acuminatum historical Panicum acuminatum varieties have contested current delimitation; seasonally variable
Steinchisma hians under Panicum hians in 1999 printed Flora
Stapfochloa species are formerly Chloris and canterae-versus-ciliata differential is not yet fully keyed
Panicum dichotomiflorum has no prior accessible rights-suitable Hays image in sample
Panicum repens and Megathyrsus maximus have no verified Hays established population
safety_guards: Never write live cards or key characteristic arrays
Never treat descriptions as Hays-specimen evidence
Never publish sources with unverified photo rights
Never count previous photo inspection as new

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Panicum hians Elliott (older name; Steinchisma subgenus)

bibliography: Flora of North Central Texas, p. 222 (file page), printed p. 1298

character_evidence.description: Perennial with upright or decumbent bases; typical flowering stems about 20–75 cm
Very short membranous ligule near 0.5 mm, its rim glabrous to finely ciliolate depending on source
Open or partially contracted panicle about 6–20 cm; lowest 1–3 cm of some branches lacks spikelets
Glabrous, approximately 1.8–2.6 mm, at maturity its tip characteristically gapes
Both glumes present; the lower generally about one-third to half the spikelet length
Inflated broadly obovate palea of lower sterile floret may protrude above its lemma; major gaping diagnostic

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Loose branched panicle with small drooping florets over lanceolate leaf blades, some contextual rocky ground photographs.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Only three images and no spikelet closeup, lemma/membrane characters or base; no independent confirmation versus related Panicum/Steinchisma.
taxa.lookalikes: Other Steinchisma/Panicum: Panicum dichotomiflorum and Panicum repens; don't confuse gaping palea with glume margins
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Get a same-plant ripe spikelet dissection that clearly shows inflated lower-floret palea, lower glume ratio and truly gaping apex, along with collar and base.
taxa.hold: Original 3 Hays source photos lack close spikelets; species ranking remains unverified.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Panicum acuminatum Sw. (historic broader concept with three varieties)

bibliography: Flora of North Central Texas PDF p. 219 printed p.1295

character_evidence.description: Perennial develops a leafy basal winter rosette, spring flowering culms and smaller crowded autumn branches
character_evidence.needed_photo: winter rosette and spring flowering stem

character_evidence.description: Spring culms tend to be less branched, bearing a more open terminal panicle
Later in season stems branch repeatedly into shorter leaves and reduced or partly sheathed panicles
Old broad Panicum acuminatum concept records blades mostly 3–12 mm wide
1999 broad-key var. acuminatum has spreading hairs about 2.5–4 mm; historic var. lindheimeri may have fewer and more ascending hairs
Historic Flora concept groups spikelets about 1–2.7 mm depending on variety; single measurement cannot prove modern species boundary

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Single leafy groundcover patch with narrow lanceolate leaves in shaded/rocky context.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: No discernible flowering panicle, spikelets, stem/leaf pubescence, winter rosette or sheath details; complex D. acuminatum taxon concept.
taxa.lookalikes: Dichanthelium lindheimeri/villosissimum and other members of the acuminatum complex
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Find a same-location winter rosette, vernal flowering specimen and hairs on sheath/node with mm scale; use a current species/variety concept and mature vernal spikelet measures.
taxa.hold: Historic var. villosum and lindheimeri combinations may have modern separate placements; do not auto-transfer their traits to a narrowly defined acuminatum. Single Hays photo is vegetative and does not resolve species.

bibliography: Flora of North Central Texas PDF p.220 printed p.1296

character_evidence.description: Coarse summer annual, stems up to roughly 1–2 m, often bent or trailing near ground
character_evidence.needed_photo: fibrous basal root system and bent nodes

character_evidence.description: Membrane about 0.5–1 mm and capped with hairs about 2 mm; longer combined ciliate lip described in some sources
Blade relatively broad and often smooth on older plants; younger leaves may be hairy
Large airy branched panicle, often 12–40 cm under Kew/GrassBase treatment
Ovate dorsally compressed spikelet around 2.4–3 mm; falls whole
Lower glume short, around one-quarter spikelet length; upper nearly full length and several-veined

taxa.lookalikes: Panicum repens, Panicum miliaceum, Urochloa spp., and tall broad-bladed annual grass seedlings
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: HIGH SOURCE ACCESS PRIORITY: obtain a rights-eligible, true Hays observation photo of a mature panicle plus same-plant root and collar; measure lower-glume length.
taxa.hold: No original source-photo pixels were previously viewable in the saved Hays sample. This dossier cannot be used as field photo verification.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Not treated as named species in 1999 regional Flora

character_evidence.description: Perennial spreads by long branching rhizomes in wet or disturbed ground; forms dense colonies
character_evidence.source: University of Florida IFAS / USFS FEIS

character_evidence.description: Tough creeping underground stems often end in sharply pointed growing tips—the torpedo feature
character_evidence.source: University of Florida IFAS / USFS FEIS

character_evidence.description: Flat to folded narrow blue-green leaves, sometimes waxy or pale
Short ciliate membrane generally around 0.5–1 mm
Open terminal panicle with ascending branches, often roughly 7–22 cm long
Small ovate, unawned spikelets approximately 2–3 mm long

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Dense green grassy mat with some thin flowering branches visible only at distance.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Rhizome/stolon structures and diagnostic spikelets absent; one image cannot resolve torpedograss.
taxa.lookalikes: Panicum dichotomiflorum, Panicum virgatum, other rhizomatous wetland grasses
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Critical target: excavate an intact sharp-pointed scaly rhizome connected to flowering stem and document spikelet size and ligule; distinguish from shallow turf runners.
taxa.hold: Single distant Hays grass photo does not reveal rhizomes, collar, or diagnostic mature spikelets. No regional Flora account for direct local comparison.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Not covered as a named species in 1999 regional Flora

character_evidence.description: Warm-season perennial tufted bunchgrass; flowering stems commonly 30–100 cm in source treatments
character_evidence.source: Texas A&M Texas Rangelands / Kew GrassBase

character_evidence.description: Usually narrow pink to purplish flowering panicle, but head color is not diagnostic alone
Spikelet has about 3–5 florets, generally lower 2–3 bisexual and upper florets reduced
character_evidence.source: Texas A&M / Flora of North America

character_evidence.description: Each mature lemma terminates in approximately 11–15 separate awns, often unequal in length
Lemma body about 3–4 mm with hairy lower margins and midvein; spikelets attached by slender pedicels
Ligule a short ring or tuft of hairs rather than a prominent membrane

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Dry grassland tuft with long hairy feathered flowering heads and good separate head details.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Individual lemma appendage number and attachment details not counted.
taxa.lookalikes: Pappophorum mucronulatum and other pappusgrasses; generic fuzzy seedheads do not prove bicolor
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Photograph one ripe detached lemma at microscope scale and count each awn, then count fertile florets and compare panicle branch density against Pappophorum mucronulatum.
taxa.hold: Source Hays photos show feathery pink heads but not 11–15 awns counted from one lemma. Taxon name is candidate until dissection.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Not directly treated as named species in 1999 Flora; historical Chloris ciliata

character_evidence.description: Tufted perennial, typically roughly 25–60 cm tall
Fringe of hairs or almost absent, not long solid membranous flap
Several digitate or spreading one-sided racemes, normally 3–5(–7), roughly 3.5–6(–8) cm long
Strongly laterally compressed spikelet 1.8–2.8 mm long; one fertile basal floret with two upper sterile florets
Fertile lemma has conspicuous hairs along middle nerve and margins, around 0.5–1.5 mm
Fertile lemma has short subapical awn about 0.9–2.7 mm; first sterile lemma often also awned

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Clear several digitate/fingerlike and strongly curved flowering branches, plus scaled rachis and collar region; good diagnostic imagery.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Exact hairy structures along rachis, sterile/terminal florets and ligule details still need close confirmation; other Chloris/Stapfochloa types occur locally.
taxa.lookalikes: Stapfochloa canterae, Stapfochloa elata, Chloris verticillata and related fingergrasses
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Dissect a single spikelet to expose one fertile plus two sterile florets, measure lemma hairs and awns, and pair with scale of branch count and hairy collar; compare directly against canterae.
taxa.hold: Genus-level windmill arrangement is shared by several local species. Most critically, modern Stapfochloa differs from some Chloris by fully ciliate lemma margins; exact species characters require formal matched comparison.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Not directly treated as named species in 1999 Flora; historical Chloris canterae

character_evidence.description: Kew accepts Stapfochloa canterae, formerly Chloris canterae, as a distinct species
Perennial tufted grass originally native to southeastern South America, introduced to Texas
Racemes commonly digitately or subdigitately clustered, sometimes somewhat pendent or curved
character_evidence.source: Kew POWO / field guide of Chaco (habit level)

character_evidence.description: Stapfochloa generally has one fertile basal floret and two to three reduced sterile florets above it
character_evidence.source: Sousa and Santos 2022 genus concept, not species-exclusive

character_evidence.description: Stapfochloa fertile lemmas have densely ciliate longitudinal margins, unlike many Chloris species
character_evidence.source: Sousa and Santos 2022 genus concept, not species-exclusive

character_evidence.description: Verified published modern key with exact canterae-versus-ciliata sterile floret and awn measurements NOT YET VERIFIED in this packet
character_evidence.source: Evidence gap – no asserted numeric diagnosis

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Very useful image set: ciliate racemes, culm node/ligule, detached spikelets and metric ruler in frame.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Precise fertile/sterile floret/awn comparison against Stapfochloa ciliata needs formal measurement.
taxa.lookalikes: Stapfochloa ciliata, Stapfochloa elata, Chloris verticillata
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Use already saved Hays mm-ruler photo to measure 1 fertile + sterile floret stack and awn insertion; find modern FNA or treatment explicitly contrasting canterae and ciliata before publishing separate key states.
taxa.hold: Kew accepted species status and Texas introduction do NOT constitute a verified Hays observation or a differential key. The reported canterae Hays photo is strong but no source-photo pixels reexamined now.

regional_flora.historic_treatment: Not directly treated by 1999 regional Flora; historical Panicum maximum

character_evidence.description: Generally robust tufted perennial, sometimes short-rhizomatous, often 75–200 cm or taller
Ciliate membrane at the blade–sheath junction
Broad linear to lanceolate blades, often 12–40 cm long, about 4–35 mm wide across variable forms
Large open oblong or pyramidal panicle roughly 12–45 cm, lower primary branches sometimes whorled
Basal sheaths can be pubescent, culm nodes may be glabrous or bearded depending on form
Panicle has individual pedicelled spikelets, not a dense solitary finger-shaped flowering branch

taxa.previous_visible_photo_features: Bunch of tall green grass and diffuse panicle visible only from a distance.
taxa.previous_absent_photo_features: Images lack spikelet close-ups, ligule/collar, and any convincing wild establishment evidence; one is nighttime landscaping.
taxa.lookalikes: Urochloa maxima historical labels, Sorghum halepense, Panicum virgatum and similar tall introduced pasture grasses
taxa.next_required_specimen_proof: Verify actual same-plant species from a ripe spikelet and inner collar, then establish whether Hays plants are landscape-planted or producing a self-sustaining population.
taxa.hold: Previous imagery is only tall landscape grass and distant open panicles, including nighttime lawn context; species ID and wild status unproven.
